paras: The Charles Mix County wife-murder lynching pursuit was a reported attempt in March 1888 by a party in Charles Mix County, Dakota Territory, to hunt down and lynch a man said to have murdered his wife. No lynching was reported, and about a week later a man accused of a wife murder in the county was reported under arrest at Wheeler.

On March 21, 1888, a special telegram from Armour, Dakota, stated that a report had come in that day that a man in Charles Mix county had "brutally murdered his wife" the night before. According to the same report, "a party" was pursuing him "with the intention of lynching him." The dispatch named neither the man nor his wife, gave no place within the county, and closed with the remark that "particulars cannot be learned."

On March 30 the Yankton Press and Daily Dakotaian carried a brief saying that a case of wife murder in Charles Mix county had been reported and that the offender, whom it called a "squaw man," was under arrest at Wheeler. The brief did not mention any pursuit or mob, and it did not name the accused, so its link to the Armour report rests on the shared county and timing. No report of an inquest, indictment or trial was found in the coverage.

The Omaha Daily Bee printed the Armour telegram on March 22 under the headline "The Murder Business in Dakota," directly after an item on the pitchfork assault on Jesse Powell at Armour, a separate case. The Bee offered no comment on the reported plan to lynch the man and presented the whole matter as an unconfirmed rumor. The Yankton brief ran in a column of one-line "Dakota Condensations," and the Bismarck Weekly Tribune repeated it word for word in its Dakota news column on April 6. Neither of these later items referred to the lynching threat.

bases: The only report of mob action is a party pursuing an accused wife murderer 'with the intention of lynching him' (A2); no killing or seizure is reported, so this is at most a threatened lynching.

A party pursued the accused intending to lynch him over an alleged wife murder (A2), but no report says he was caught or killed by it, and a week later a man accused of a Charles Mix county wife murder was reported under arrest at Wheeler (A5). The size of the party is not given.

Only one telegram reports the lynching pursuit (A2); the Yankton brief (A5, reprinted in A7) reports a wife murder and arrest in the same county but does not mention a mob and does not confirm it is the same case.
